output.risk_summary: Combining ibuprofen (Advil) with alcohol significantly increases your risk of stomach bleeding and can cause serious liver and kidney damage.

details.finding: Alcohol and ibuprofen taken together greatly increase the chance of stomach bleeding
details.explanation: Ibuprofen is an anti-inflammatory painkiller (NSAID) that can irritate your stomach lining and make it more vulnerable to bleeding. Alcohol does the same thing. When you combine them, the risk multiplies — you could develop bleeding ulcers or dangerous gastrointestinal bleeding that might not show obvious symptoms until it becomes serious. This is especially risky if you drink regularly or take ibuprofen for several days in a row.
details.source: FDA NSAID safety guidance and alcohol interaction warnings

details.finding: Alcohol combined with ibuprofen puts extra strain on your liver and kidneys
details.explanation: Both alcohol and ibuprofen are processed by your liver and filtered by your kidneys. Taking them together forces these organs to work much harder, which can lead to liver inflammation or reduced kidney function over time. If you already have any liver or kidney problems, even mild ones you might not know about, this combination becomes particularly dangerous.
details.source: FDA NSAID safety guidance and alcohol interaction warnings

output.what_to_do: Do not take Advil (ibuprofen) if you have been drinking alcohol or plan to drink within the next several hours. If you need pain relief and have consumed alcohol, acetaminophen (Tylenol) is generally safer, but you must stay within 3,000mg per day total and avoid it entirely if you drink three or more alcoholic drinks daily. The safest approach is to wait until the alcohol has completely cleared your system — at least 4 to 6 hours after your last drink — before taking any pain medication. If you regularly drink alcohol and also need regular pain relief, talk to a pharmacist about which option is safest for your specific situation and whether you should avoid NSAIDs like ibuprofen altogether.
